data.hypothesis: The selected SSE2 parent is valid and measured 5.631 ms versus the 7.529 ms scalar baseline, but its per-lane logf/expf calls may limit SIMD throughput. Replacing those calls with guarded SSE2 polynomial log/exp approximations may reduce that cost while retaining the supplied Black-Scholes formula and CND coefficients. Unsafe input ranges, tails, and builds without SSE2 use the scalar implementation. This tests the remaining scalar-math bottleneck; speed and tolerance compliance remain unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: This applies to the recorded benchmark and its tested cases; it does not establish performance or tolerance for this new approximation.
memory_lessons.claim: The guarded four-lane SSE2 parent was correct on eight varied cases and measured 5.631 ms, compared with 7.529 ms for the scalar baseline. Its implementation still called scalar logf and expf per lane.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a guarded SSE2 vector-math route against both recorded programs, with correctness checks over varied sizes and seeds.

data.notes: Only src/candidate.cpp is changed; threading and compiler settings are unchanged. The parent-versus-baseline measurements are prior controller results, not measurements of this candidate. The controller should validate the approximation against tolerance on varied inputs and measure its performance.
transformations: Added SSE2 polynomial approximations for log and exp to remove per-lane scalar transcendental calls on safe ranges.
Retained the original arithmetic structure and supplied CND coefficients in the vector kernel.
Fell back to the scalar serial routine for non-normal ratios, unsafe exponential ranges, unsupported builds, and vector tails.
Kept threading, compiler flags, and the run entrypoint unchanged.
